title: Open a coupler knuckle by hand, then roll the car in until the knuckle closes and locks
instruction: Couple the red car to the grey coupler head and leave them locked together.
context: Yard crews open a coupler knuckle by hand before cars are shoved together: two closed knuckles butt and push the cars apart, and the lock pin dropping is the check that the coupling took (O*NET 53-4022.00 Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators and Locomotive Firers; 53-4031.00 Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters). Crews never stand between cars during a shove; the simulation cannot score where the arms are, so that is a rule for real trials. Closest board tasks hold a release with one hand while the other moves a part, or close a sprung gate; this one adds a mechanism that must be set before a shove and that the shove then closes and locks on its own.
setup: Positions are cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); z is height above the table top. Table: wood top, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. All parts below form one fixed mock-up on a track along y. Track bed: dark plastic, 6 x 40 x 2 cm tall, fixed, x 24 to 30, y -20 to 20. Coupler head: grey plastic, fixed, x 23.5 to 30.5, y -14 to -6, z 2 to 8, with a throat open toward the car, 3.0 cm wide (x 25.6 to 28.6) and 3.5 cm deep (y -9.5 to -6). Slideway: grey plastic, 10 x 3.2 x 3 cm tall, fixed, x 28.5 to 38.5, y -5.8 to -2.6. Knuckle jaw: black plastic slab 5.65 x 2.4 x 4 cm tall (shut: x 27.85 to 33.5, y -5.4 to -3.0, z 3 to 7), sliding along x on the slideway, 2.5 cm of travel toward +x, 50 g; its top has a 1.8 cm square notch 0.8 cm deep (shut: x 30.85 to 32.65, y -5.1 to -3.3) and a black ramp plate 4.6 x 1 x 2 cm tall (z 3 to 5) on its front, sloping 26.6 degrees from the x axis (its surface passes x 31.4, y -2.4 and falls 1 cm in y per 2 cm in x). Shut, its tip lies 4.5 mm over the edge of the pin head. Lever: red plastic bar 1 x 14.4 x 2 cm tall on the jaw's +x end (x 33.5 to 34.5, y -5.4 to 9, z 3 to 5), with a red grip block 1.8 x 3 x 3 cm tall at its tip (x 33.1 to 34.9, y 6 to 9, z 3 to 6). Lock: yellow plastic, 30 g, sliding vertically up to 3 cm on a spring (100 N/m): a 1.2 cm square foot and post (z 6.2 to 10) standing in the notch at x 31.75, y -4.2, and a grip tab 3 x 1.8 x 3 cm tall on top (x 30.25 to 33.25, y -5.1 to -3.3, z 10 to 13). Car: red plastic body 6 x 7 x 6 cm tall (x 24 to 30, y 15 to 22, z 2 to 8), 300 g, sliding along y on the bed, 15 cm of travel toward the head; a black necked pin on its nose (neck 0.8 x 7 x 4 cm tall, head 2.4 x 1 x 4 cm tall, tip at y 7); a red striker finger 1 x 10.3 x 2 cm tall (x 31.95 to 32.95, y 11.7 to 22, z 3 to 5) on its right, joined to the body by a bridge at the rear; a blue push handle 3 x 3 x 5 cm tall on its left (x 21 to 24, y 17 to 20, z 4 to 9). Coupled, the pin head lies in the throat with its tip at y -7.35 and the jaw shut behind it. A shut jaw stops the pin head 10 cm short of that.
scoring: At the end of the run, grippers open; read from a top photo and a ruler. K: how far the jaw is pulled open (cm). L: how far the lock is lifted above its notch floor (mm). J: how far the car has moved toward the head (cm). Coupled: K 3 mm or less, L 3 mm or less, and J 13.35 to 15.35 cm. Butt: J 9.2 to 10.8 cm while K was 3 mm or less, at any time. 1.0: coupled, no butt, still for 1 s. 0.75: coupled after a butt, or coupled but not yet still for 1 s. 0.5: not coupled, but at any time K was 2 cm or more while J was under 2 cm. 0.25: otherwise, L was 1.2 cm or more for 0.5 s at any time. Else 0. A jaw shut by hand with the pin not seated is not coupled; a lock held up at the end is not dropped. Where the arms are is not scored.
reset_notes: Slide the car back to its start (pin tip at y 7), push the jaw shut and let the lock drop into its notch. Mark the car's nose and the jaw's tip on the track with tape.
fidelity: Approximate. The knuckle is a sliding jaw, shut by a striker finger on a ramp, not a swinging one; the lock is a sprung sliding pin; air hoses and real car mass are not modelled. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a lock still held up (over 3 mm above its notch floor) counts as not dropped, and the car cannot leave its track.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved arms near the track, never moved the car or the knuckle); demo: 1.0 (right arm opened the knuckle, left arm pushed the car into the head, both arms retreated)
